Distribution and biology. (Fig. 58). Central Nepal. Adults have been collected in March (1, 22. iii), April (2, 12. iv), June (11. vi) 1990 and 1992 (type series), July and late August (ZSM material) at elevations of 1200 – 1800 m, at Mt. Pulchouki near Godavari village, vicinity of Kathmandu. Probably bivoltine, moths occuring in hillside broadleaved forest. The larvae and foodplants are unknown.

Distribution. The species is known from the Northern Territory and Queensland, from Pine Creek (north-west of Katherine) and northern Kakadu National Park (near the South Alligator River) in the north to near Brisbane in southern Queensland (Figs. 69 – 70). Host-plants. The type series was largely collected from Acacia holosericea and A. leptocarpa, at Pungalina, with fewer specimens from A. dimidiata and A. hammondii and (in Queensland) singletons from A. leiocalyx and A. triptera (Table 1). The first two Acacia species occur throughout the known distribution of M. psittacoides, whereas A. dimidiata and A. hammondii are limited to the Northern Territory and northern Queensland and A. leiocalyx and A. triptera to southern Queensland and northern New South Wales (Table 1).
